verses.22:1: O Senhor {regit}, e nada me faltará: * num lugar de {pascuae} ali me {collocavit}.
verses.22:3: Guiou-me {semitas} da justiça, * por causa do seu nome.
verses.22:4: Pois, ainda que eu ande no meio da sombra da morte, {mala}: * porque vós estais comigo.
verses.22:4b: A vossa vara, e o vosso {baculus}: * {ipsa} me consolaram.
verses.22:5b: {impinguasti} a minha cabeça: * e o meu cálice {inebrians}, {praeclarus}!
verses.22:6: E a vossa misericórdia {subsequetur} * todos os dias da minha vida:

decisions.why: The best-known line of the psalter in Brazil is the Hebrew family's: 'O SENHOR é o meu pastor, nada me falta' (CNBB, read in consult/bolls-CNBB-19-23.json). The Latin does not say 'shepherd': it says regit, 'keeps straight, guides, directs, governs' (Lewis & Short, rego I). The Greek behind it is ποιμαίνει ('shepherds'), and in the Latin psalter the same verb carries the shepherd's sense in 79:2 'Qui regis Israël … qui dedúcis velut ovem Joseph' — so the pastoral colour is the Latin's too, but through a verb of ruling, not a noun of flock. The glossary row régere → reger (open; 2:9 'Tu os regerás') named this verse; régere has three places in the psalter (2:9, 22:1, 79:2 — grep), and one Portuguese verb keeps them one. Douay-Rheims 'The Lord ruleth me'; Matos Soares 1932 'O Senhor me governa'. The line is also a versicle: DO's Sunday Sext has 'V. Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit. R. In loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.' (Psalterium/Special/Minor Special.txt, [Versum Dominica Sexta]) — each half must stand as a sentence, and does. The weight of the familiar wording is real: 'O Senhor é o meu pastor' is what nearly every Brazilian will expect, and hearing another line at the head of this psalm will surprise. It is refused because it translates the Hebrew's noun (rō'î), not the Latin's verb (rule 1); it stays one touch away.

options.label: me rege
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's verb (2:9 'regerás', 79:2 will be 'que regeis Israel'); the Latin's own word, current in Portuguese (reger um povo, uma orquestra); 'O Senhor me rege' is short, stressed like the Latin, and still says guidance as well as rule.

options.label: é o meu pastor
options.note: The familiar Brazilian wording (CNBB 'O SENHOR é o meu pastor'); the Greek's shepherding made a noun. It translates the Hebrew family, not the Latin (rule 1); kept for its weight in the ear of every Brazilian.

options.label: me governa
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 (DRB 'ruleth'): the Latin's sense of rule; 'governar' is political in Brazil, and loses the guiding.

options.label: me conduz
options.note: Lewis & Short's 'lead, guide, conduct'; the shepherd's motion without the noun. Loses the link with 2:9 and 79:2, and sits close to 22:3's 'Guiou-me' (dedúcere).

options.label: me apascenta
options.note: The Greek's verb (ποιμαίνει) exactly — the shepherd without the noun; not the Latin's verb (rule 1), and literary.

decisions.why: páscua: 'pasture'. It returns in the formula 'oves páscuæ' (73:1, 78:13, 99:3b) and the Invitatory's 'pópulus páscuæ ejus' (94:7) — grep — so the word must serve 'o povo da sua pastagem' too. Douay-Rheims 'a place of pasture'; Matos Soares 1932 'num lugar de pastos'. The half-verse is sung alone as an antiphon: Thursday Prime 'In loco páscuæ * ibi Dóminus me collocávit' (Psalterium/Psalmi/Psalmi minor.txt) and the Office of the Dead 'In loco páscuæ * ibi me collocávit' (Commune/C9.txt).

options.label: pastagem
options.note: Ruling: the plain collective noun, singular as the Latin; serves 94:7 ('o povo da sua pastagem').

options.label: pastos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's plural; as plain, but the Latin is singular.

decisions.why: collocáre: 'to place, set, settle'. The Greek is κατεσκήνωσεν ('made me dwell, pitch a tent'), the Latin a verb of placing — the Latin is followed. 'ibi' resumes 'in loco páscuæ' and is kept ('ali'), as the Latin repeats the place. Four places in the psalter (22:1, 103:22, 106:36, 142:3b — grep); 'colocar' serves 106:36 and 142:3b as well. 'estabelecer' is constitúere's, 'pôr' pónere's.

options.label: colocou
options.note: Ruling: the cognate, plain (Matos Soares 1932 'colocou-me'); ends on an oxytone.

options.label: fez morar
options.note: The Greek's sense (κατεσκήνωσεν) — against rule 1.

options.label: estabeleceu
options.note: Settled as a dwelling; but constitúere's verb in this psalter.

decisions.why: super + accusative of place: 'over, upon', and 'by, near' (as 136:1 'Super flúmina Babylónis', by the rivers). The Greek ἐπὶ ὕδατος. Douay-Rheims 'on the water'; Matos Soares 1932 'junto duma água'. 'Sobre a água' in Portuguese sets the speaker on top of the water.

options.label: Junto à
options.note: Ruling: the sense of place, as Matos Soares 1932; the singular 'água' kept.

options.label: Sobre a
options.note: Douay-Rheims 'on the water': the preposition to the letter; heard as on the water's surface.

decisions.why: refectio: 'a restoring … refreshment, recreation, recovery' (Lewis & Short). Only here in the psalter (grep). The Greek is ἀναπαύσεως, 'of rest'; the Latin says restoring, and is followed. The Portuguese cognate 'refeição' is a meal, and would say something the Latin does not. Douay-Rheims 'water of refreshment'; Matos Soares 1932 'uma água fortificante' (an adjective).

options.label: água do refrigério
options.note: Ruling: 'refrigério' is relief and refreshment, the Latin's noun kept as a noun; a word of prayer in Brazil. The blind reader is asked whether it is known.

options.label: água do repouso
options.note: The Greek's 'rest' (ἀναπαύσεως) — against rule 1.

options.label: água que restaura
options.note: The first sense of refectio as a clause; plainer, but a noun becomes a verb.

decisions.why: educávit is ēducáre (first conjugation), 'to bring up, rear, nourish' — not ēdúcere, 'to lead out'. The Greek is ἐξέθρεψέν με, 'nurtured me'. Douay-Rheims 'He hath brought me up'; Matos Soares 1932 'Conduziu-me' reads ēdúcere, which the form excludes. 'me criou' is the Brazilian 'raised me', but with God as subject it is heard first as 'created me'; 'me educou' is heard as schooling or manners.

options.label: me nutriu
options.note: Ruling: the rearing as nourishment, the Greek's ἐξέθρεψεν exactly and the first thing ēducáre does to a child; cannot be heard as 'created'.

options.label: me criou
options.note: 'raised me', the plain Brazilian verb for rearing; with God as subject it is heard first as 'created me'.

options.label: me educou
options.note: The cognate: heard as schooling or manners.

options.label: me conduziu
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: reads ēdúcere ('lead out') against the form of the verb.

decisions.why: convértere → voltar (glossary), with D25's one exception, 'converter' where the sense is conversion to God; Ps 18:8 'convértens ánimas' → 'converte as almas' took that exception for God acting on souls, which is this verse's build exactly (ἐπέστρεψεν). Douay-Rheims 'he hath converted my soul'; Matos Soares 1932 'converteu a minha alma'. The Hebrew-family 'restaura' is refused (rule 1). The Latin puts the object first; Portuguese order is taken (D2).

options.label: converteu a minha alma
options.note: Ruling: 18:8's verb (D25's exception), both Vulgate-family versions.

options.label: fez voltar a minha alma
options.note: The glossary's plain verb as a causative; keeps the turning, loses 18:8's echo.

options.label: a minha alma converteu
options.note: The Latin's order, verb last: an inversion.

decisions.why: dedúcere, 'deduc me' → guiar (D22, settled); sémita → vereda (D15). super + accusative with a verb of leading: 'along, over'. Douay-Rheims 'on the paths of justice'; Matos Soares 1932 'por veredas de justiça'. The article is kept before the genitive ('da justiça'), as the Latin's justítiæ is the paths' definite quality.

options.label: pelas veredas
options.note: Ruling: the preposition Portuguese uses with a road after a verb of leading.

options.label: sobre as veredas
options.note: super to the letter; not how a road is walked in Portuguese.

decisions.why: mala is plural, 'evils' (κακά). Douay-Rheims 'I will fear no evils'; Matos Soares 1932 'não temerei males'. The familiar 'não temerei mal algum' (CNBB 'não temerei mal nenhum') is singular and turns the object into 'any evil at all'; the plural is the Latin's. 'Nam, et si ambulávero' (future perfect) → 'ainda que eu ande' (the Portuguese present subjunctive of a condition); ambuláre → andar (glossary).

options.label: não temerei males
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's plural, bare as the Latin (Matos Soares 1932 word for word).

options.label: não temerei mal algum
options.note: The familiar wording: the plural made 'any evil'; smoother, but a change of number and an added emphasis.

decisions.why: virga → vara (glossary: 'must serve 22:4'). báculus: 'a stick, staff' (the Greek βακτηρία, a walking staff); only here in the psalter (grep). The cognate 'báculo' is in Brazil the bishop's crozier, a proparoxytone at the mediant, and heard as a church object. 'cajado' is the shepherd's staff in every Brazilian ear, and a paroxytone. The first colon stays verbless, as the Latin: a hanging pair resumed by 'ipsa'.

options.label: cajado
options.note: Ruling: the plain word for a staff to lean on and to guide with.

options.label: bordão
options.note: The walking staff (the pilgrim's); exact for βακτηρία, less current.

options.label: báculo
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the cognate, heard as a bishop's crozier; a proparoxytone at the mediant (rule 4).

decisions.why: ipsa (neuter plural) resumes the rod and the staff: 'they, those very things'. The Latin repeats the subject, and so does the Portuguese; the gender follows Portuguese agreement (vara + cajado → masculine plural). Douay-Rheims 'they have comforted me'; Matos Soares 1932 drops the pronoun ('A tua vara e o teu báculo me consolaram').

options.label: eles
options.note: Ruling: the resumptive pronoun kept, plain.

options.label: esses mesmos
options.note: ipsa's emphasis spelled out; heavier.

options.label: foram eles que
options.note: A cleft for the emphasis; adds a construction.

decisions.why: in conspéctu → à vista de (glossary row conspéctus, open), which Ps 5's agent tried on this very verse ('Preparastes à minha vista uma mesa') and found that it holds; Ps 17 found 'à vista' right as a place of seeing and 'na presença' where it hangs beside a noun. Here it goes with a verb of preparing, not of motion. The Latin's order (the phrase before the object) is kept, so that 'uma mesa' closes the colon as 'mensam' does. Douay-Rheims 'before me'; Matos Soares 1932 'diante de mim'.

options.label: à minha vista
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's noun, tried here by Ps 5.

options.label: diante de mim
options.note: Both Vulgate-family versions and the familiar ear; the noun of sight lost.

options.label: na minha presença
options.note: Ps 17's form beside a noun.

decisions.why: advérsus: 'over against, facing; against'. The Greek ἐξ ἐναντίας, 'in the face of'. Douay-Rheims 'against them that afflict me'; Matos Soares 1932 'à vista daqueles que me perseguem' (which would repeat 'à vista' in one verse). tribuláre → atribular (glossary).

options.label: contra os que
options.note: Ruling: Douay-Rheims 'against' — the table set as a challenge to the enemies.

options.label: em face dos que
options.note: The Greek's 'in the face of' (ἐξ ἐναντίας): the place, not the hostility.

decisions.why: impinguáre: 'to make fat' (Lewis & Short, glossing πιαίνω); the Greek here is ἐλίπανας, 'oiled, anointed with fat'. Two places: 22:5 and 140:5 'óleum autem peccatóris non impínguet caput meum' (grep). The image is the host pouring oil on a guest's head; Douay-Rheims 'Thou hast anointed my head with oil' (but 'fatten' at 140:5); Matos Soares 1932 'Ungiste com óleo'. Cost: 'ungir' is also úngere's (44:8 'unxit te Deus … óleo lætítiæ', 88:21 — grep), another verb (χρίω) — the two never stand in one psalm, and no plainer Portuguese keeps impinguáre's fat without absurdity ('Engordastes'). 'Untastes' keeps the fat (unto) and stays apart from úngere, but is the verb of greasing a pan.

options.label: Ungistes com óleo
options.note: Ruling: the oil on the head, as every Vulgate-family version; shares 'ungir' with úngere (44:8, 88:21).

options.label: Untastes com óleo
options.note: Keeps the fat of impinguáre ('untar', from 'unto') and stays apart from úngere; a kitchen verb in Brazil.

options.label: Engordastes com óleo
options.note: The Latin verb to the letter; heard as absurd.

decisions.why: inebriáre: 'to make drunk' — the cup that inebriates; the image kept, unexplained (the Fathers read it of the Eucharist; the verse does not say so). calix → cálice (glossary; not at a cadence here). inebriáre elsewhere 35:9, 64:10, 64:11 (grep). Douay-Rheims 'my chalice which inebriateth me'; Matos Soares 1932 'o meu cálice que embriaga'.

options.label: que embriaga
options.note: Ruling: the participle as a relative clause (Matos Soares 1932); the plain verb.

options.label: inebriante
options.note: The participle kept as an adjective; current, but heard of perfumes.

decisions.why: præclárus → excelente (glossary, 15:6 twice; the row names this verse). quam exclamatory → 'Como …!' (glossary, working: 8:2a, 118:97). Douay-Rheims 'how goodly is it!'; Matos Soares 1932 'quão precioso é'.

options.label: como é excelente
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's two rows; ends on a paroxytone.

options.label: quão excelente é
options.note: The præclárus row's own proposal; 'quão' is the bookish option of the quam row.

decisions.why: subséqui: 'to follow close after'; only here in the psalter (grep). The Greek is καταδιώξεταί με, 'will pursue me' — the Latin softens it to following, and is followed. Douay-Rheims 'will follow me'; Matos Soares 1932 'irá após de mim'.

options.label: me seguirá
options.note: Ruling: the plain verb; the sub- (close behind) is not heard.

options.label: me acompanhará
options.note: Walking with, not after.

options.label: me perseguirá
options.note: The Greek's 'pursue' — against rule 1, and heard as hostile.

decisions.latin: Et ut inhábitem in domo Dómini
decisions.why: A purpose clause hanging on the verse before (mercy will follow me … and so that I may dwell), as the Latin and the Greek (τὸ κατοικεῖν με) leave it; the Hebrew-family 'e habitarei' is refused (rule 1). Douay-Rheims 'And that I may dwell'; Matos Soares 1932 'a fim de que eu habite'. inhabitáre → habitar (16 lines, grep). 26:4 'ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ' is a near twin and should copy.

options.label: E para que eu habite
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's clause, the subject named (the subjunctive would not show it).

options.label: E a fim de que eu habite

forms.ut: E a fim de que eu habite

options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the same, heavier.

options.label: E habitarei
options.note: The Hebrew family's future (CNBB and the familiar ear) — against rule 1.

decisions.why: longitúdo diérum → longos dias (glossary, working: 90:16 'Eu o encherei de longos dias', 20:5 'e lhe destes longos dias'); the row named this verse and 92:5 (the other 'in longitúdinem diérum', grep) as its tests. in + accusative of extent: 'unto, for'. Douay-Rheims 'unto length of days'; Matos Soares 1932 'durante longos dias'.

options.label: por longos dias
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's phrase with the preposition of duration.

options.label: durante longos dias
options.note: Matos Soares 1932; heavier.

options.label: para longos dias
options.note: in + accusative as direction; heard as 'in view of'.

choices.22:1: The psalm speaks of God in the third person until 22:4 turns to him (vós). 'nihil mihi déerit' (future) → 'nada me faltará' (Matos Soares 1932; the Hebrew family's present 'nada me falta' is refused). 'ibi' kept as 'ali'. The two halves are said apart as V/R at Sunday Sext and as an antiphon at Thursday Prime and in the Office of the Dead (checked in DO).
choices.22:3: dedúcere → guiar (D22, 'deduc me'): the perfect 'Guiou-me'. 'propter nomen suum' → 'por causa do seu nome' (glossary propter).
choices.22:4: 'quóniam tu mecum es' → 'porque vós estais comigo' (D1). The familiar 'porque tu estás comigo' is the address the project does not use for God.
choices.22:4b: virga → vara (glossary). The Latin's hanging nominative kept, resumed by the pronoun.
choices.22:5: tribuláre → atribular (glossary; the blind reader of Ps 3 did not know it, kept).
choices.22:6: The verse ends on a colon in the Latin, and so does the Portuguese: 22:6b depends on it.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm22.txt: nine prayed verses, of which DO numbers two each as 22:4, 22:5 and 22:6. The shared scripts key verses by id, so the repeated ids collapse; this psalm uses 22:4/22:4b, 22:5/22:5b, 22:6/22:6b (DO's own form for a split verse, as 4:2a/4:2b) and runs render.py and checks.py through ps022/dupids.py, which letters the repeated ids without touching the shared scripts. No titulus (D7). DO's other uses checked by grep over content/do/horas/Latin: 22:1 is the Sunday Sext versicle split at the asterisk (Psalterium/Special/Minor Special.txt); 'In loco páscuæ * ibi (Dóminus) me collocávit' is the Thursday Prime antiphon (Psalmi minor.txt) and an antiphon of the Office of the Dead (Commune/C9.txt); 'Dóminus regit me * et nihil mihi déerit: in loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit' is a Matins antiphon (Psalmi matutinum.txt).

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps022.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932; this psalm has no Diurnal Monástico text in the parallels). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). CNBB read in consult/bolls-CNBB-19-23.json for the familiar wording only. Lewis & Short read for rego, refectio, impinguo. Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py: régere (22:1, 79:2, and 2:9 'reges'), collocáre (4 lines), páscua (6), subséqui (1), refectio (1), ēducáre (22:2; 103:14 'edúcas' is ēdúcere), báculus (1), impinguáre (2), inebriáre (4), longitúdo diérum (4), inhabitáre (16). Latin readings kept against the Hebrew: 22:1 'me rege' (not 'shepherd'), 'nada me faltará' (future), 22:2 'água do refrigério' (restoring), 'me nutriu', 'converteu a minha alma', 22:4 'males', 22:5b 'o meu cálice que embriaga, como é excelente', 22:6 'me seguirá' (the Greek pursues), 22:6b 'E para que eu habite' (not 'I shall dwell'). 18 decisions.

Draft 1: hard pass (run through ps022/dupids.py: DO's Psalm22.txt repeats 22:4, 22:5, 22:6, which the shared scripts collapse; ids lettered 22:4/22:4b … as DO's own 4:2a/4:2b). Soft flags accepted: 22:5b second colon +4 (the relative 'que embriaga' for the participle, and 'como é' for quam … est); 22:6b second colon −4 ('por longos dias' for 'in longitúdinem diérum'; 'pela longura dos dias' keeps the noun but is not current Portuguese). No rhyme flag. Every mediant and final lands on an oxytone or paroxytone.
